plan.planning_summary: This plan initiates the first of two allowed research rounds for designing a two-layer antireflection coating. Since no literature evidence is available, the routes are theory-based, relying on thin-film interference principles. Two complementary routes are proposed to resolve the primary method research question: which layer ordering (SiO2/TiO2 vs. TiO2/SiO2) yields the lower global minimum reflectance within the specified thickness bounds (40-160 nm). Route 01 tests the high-index-first topology, while Route 02 tests the low-index-first topology. Both routes utilize deterministic TMM optimization with a fixed seed and evaluation budget.

routes.title: Optimization of TiO2/SiO2/Glass Stack
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Placing the higher refractive index material (TiO2) adjacent to the air incident medium and the lower index material (SiO2) adjacent to the glass substrate will yield a lower arithmetic mean reflectance over the 450-700 nm band compared to the reverse order, given the specific thickness constraints of 40-160 nm.
routes.design_principle: Impedance matching via stepped refractive index profile (Air -> High -> Low -> Substrate) to minimize Fresnel reflections at interfaces, optimized for broadband performance within geometric constraints.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | TiO2 (Layer 1) | SiO2 (Layer 2) | Glass Substrate. Total finite layers: 2.
soft_objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance (s-pol, normal incidence) from 450 nm to 700 nm
manufacturing_considerations: Layer thicknesses must strictly remain between 40 nm and 160 nm
theory_basis: Thin-film interference theory suggests that a high-low index sequence can provide better broadband matching for high-index substrates than low-high, depending on the specific index values and wavelength range.
Quarter-wave approximation provides an initial guess, but broadband minimization requires deviation from single-wavelength quarter-wave conditions.
expected_advantages: Potentially smoother spectral response due to the gradual index transition from Air (1.0) to TiO2 (2.40) to SiO2 (1.46) to Glass (1.52).
TiO2 as the first layer may offer stronger phase control for the short wavelengths in the band.
known_risks: The large index jump from Air to TiO2 might create a strong reflection peak that the second layer cannot fully suppress within the thickness limits.
The optimal solution might lie on the boundary of the thickness constraints (40 or 160 nm), limiting further improvement.
routes.execution_request_english: Execute a deterministic TMM optimization for a planar stack: Incident Medium Air (n=1.0), Layer 1 TiO2 (n=2.40, lossless), Layer 2 SiO2 (n=1.46, lossless), Substrate Glass (n=1.52, lossless). Illumination: Normal incidence (0 deg), s-polarization. Wavelength range: 450 nm to 700 nm, sampled every 5 nm. Objective: Minimize the arithmetic mean of power reflectance across the sampled wavelengths. Design variables: Thickness of Layer 1 and Layer 2, both bounded between 40 nm and 160 nm. Optimization settings: Maximum 64 solver evaluations, random seed 17. Output the optimal thicknesses, the full reflectance spectrum, the calculated mean reflectance, and the best target score. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees. polarization s. wavelength intervals 450-700 nm. soft objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 nm to 700 nm; achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflection in the 450 nm to 700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: layer thickness must be between 40 nm and 160 nm; exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2.

routes.title: Optimization of SiO2/TiO2/Glass Stack
routes.scientific_hypothesis: Placing the lower refractive index material (SiO2) adjacent to the air incident medium and the higher index material (TiO2) adjacent to the glass substrate will yield a lower arithmetic mean reflectance over the 450-700 nm band compared to the reverse order, given the specific thickness constraints of 40-160 nm.
routes.design_principle: Impedance matching via stepped refractive index profile (Air -> Low -> High -> Substrate), leveraging the SiO2 layer to reduce the initial air-interface reflection before the TiO2 layer matches to the substrate.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | SiO2 (Layer 1) | TiO2 (Layer 2) | Glass Substrate. Total finite layers: 2.
soft_objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance (s-pol, normal incidence) from 450 nm to 700 nm
manufacturing_considerations: Layer thicknesses must strictly remain between 40 nm and 160 nm
theory_basis: Standard V-coat or broadband AR designs often place a lower index material first to mitigate the large index mismatch between air and the subsequent high-index layer.
For a substrate index of 1.52, a low-high sequence might provide a more monotonic effective index gradient.
expected_advantages: Reduced reflection at the air-interface due to the smaller index step (1.0 to 1.46).
Potentially better performance at longer wavelengths where the quarter-wave condition shifts.
known_risks: The intermediate high-index layer (TiO2) might create a resonant cavity effect that increases reflectance at specific wavelengths within the band.
May struggle to suppress reflection at the short-wavelength end (450 nm) if the required thicknesses exceed the 160 nm limit.

Illumination: Normal incidence (0 deg), s-polarization. Wavelength range: 450 nm to 700 nm, sampled every 5 nm. Objective: Minimize the arithmetic mean of power reflectance across the sampled wavelengths. Design variables: Thickness of Layer 1 and Layer 2, both bounded between 40 nm and 160 nm. Optimization settings: Maximum 64 solver evaluations, random seed 17. Output the optimal thicknesses, the full reflectance spectrum, the calculated mean reflectance, and the best target score. Canonical user controls: incidence angles 0 degrees. polarization s. wavelength intervals 450-700 nm. soft objectives: minimize arithmetic mean power reflectance from 450 nm to 700 nm; achieve mean reflectance below 0.03 as a soft scoring preference. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflection in the 450 nm to 700 nm band. manufacturing constraints: layer thickness must be between 40 nm and 160 nm; exactly one layer of SiO2 and one layer of TiO2.

research_influence: The absence of literature evidence (evidence_ids_allowed is empty) necessitates a theory-based approach comparing the two possible topological permutations directly via optimization.

The strict limit of two research rounds dictates that both possible layer orders must be evaluated efficiently; hence, two parallel routes are defined to ensure the 'which order' question is answered definitively after Round 1 execution.
unresolved_decisions: The optimal layer ordering (SiO2-first vs. TiO2-first) remains unknown and is the primary variable to be resolved by these routes.
Whether the 0.03 mean reflectance target is physically achievable with only two layers and the given thickness constraints is unknown.
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: Stop after the bounded route portfolio is exhausted or further search stagnates. Return every physically verified candidate and report soft objective trade-offs without a performance admission threshold.
